name: Grover Cleveland
summary: A Democrat who favoured tariff reduction, sound money with a gold standard, civil service merit appointments and a limited federal government, and who opposed federal aid to individuals and the annexation of Hawaii. He also ordered federal troops into the 1894 railroad strike and pushed the Venezuela boundary dispute under the Monroe Doctrine.

notes:
Texts are the National Archives transcripts as published by the Miller Center. The presidency.ucsb.edu copies were not downloaded. Many statements have no recorded position in his messages. Answers are for his presidential-era positions, mostly from his own official messages and vetoes. Inferences are marked low.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 30 answers taken from it, 18 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent full-list pass using two complete later works as well as the complete annual messages. Post-presidential suffrage opposition is explicit. Indigenous allotment enthusiasm is qualified by his later reservations about premature allotment and sales, while his 1896 proposal still sought ending tribal courts and common ownership. Public homestead distribution does not establish redistributing private estates or community land tenure; priority items remain null. Religious analogies and invocations do not establish the requested theology of political power. No historical inference used.
